US October payrolls at 14:30 CET, consensus +65,000 and unemployment 4.2%. [6]
Sint Maarten parade in Brunssum's Langeberg; the Dutch Mountain Film Festival opens; Marres is free 17:00–20:00. [7, 8, 9]
Fog first, then cloud; GLOW Eindhoven opens at 18:30, free. Canes host Chicago, Sun 02:00 CET. [1, 10, 11]

five.t: **The Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the S&P 500 4.4%** in an AI and chip sell-off; the VIX jumped 70% to 28.18 while the AEX lost only 0.6%.
**Five US agencies told cold-chain operators to assume they are targets,** as DoD looks at freezer failures in about six commissaries; the Kremlin calls the accusations “absurd”.
**Trump on Iran: “maybe I'll have to”** destroy the rest of the country; Tehran sent a nuclear proposal through Qatar with seven conditions, and Brent rose 3.9% to $98.29.
**Hegseth: “We will not back down”;** Massie refiles impeachment articles next week, and the Europe force-level options are due today.
**Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 European flights on a third day,** one of them landing at Brussels; no device has been found.

pick.t: If you read one thing: the cold-chain lead. The US guidance and the commissary probe bring the fridge attacks onto US installations, where force protection and host-nation support meet.

items.h: Melania Trump hosts both sides on Oleshky as Trump meets Putin's envoy
items.body: At the White House on 5 Nov the First Lady hosted Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and, for Ukraine, faction leader Davyd Arakhamia and ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets; she said nearly 800 people were evacuated from Oleshky during the October truce: “Let Oleshky be the modest spark that grows into a lasting flame of peace.” [12] President Trump met Dmitriev separately: “There's going to be an agreement. It's going to be a big agreement, and it's going to involve more than Ukraine.” [13] Talks on security guarantees ended a second day at NATO headquarters without an announced outcome. [14] Overnight into 5 Nov Russia launched 128 drones and two Kh-35 missiles, 105 drones downed; Zelensky put the Komyshuvakha toll at 43. [15, 16]
items.next: US–Russia–Ukraine working-level talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov; Zelensky's full ZDF interview airs today. [14]

items.h: Iran sends a nuclear proposal through Qatar; Trump says “maybe I'll have to” destroy the rest
items.body: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on 5 Nov that Iran had sent the US a nuclear proposal through Qatar, to be discussed only after Washington meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions, releasing frozen assets and paying reparations. [17] After meeting his national security team, President Trump said: “I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I'll have to. You'll know soon enough.” [18] The Revolutionary Guards said three tankers were damaged in the strait on 5 Nov; no ship was named. Lloyd's List counted 116 non-Iranian-linked transits in the week to 25 Oct, down from 124. [19, 20]
items.next: No date is set for direct talks; Lloyd's List publishes its next Hormuz brief on 19 Nov. [20]

items.h: Colom's lead in Mississippi widens to 1,882; Peltola leads Alaska by 637
items.body: The Mississippi Free Press put Scott Colom 1,882 votes ahead of Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith on the evening of 5 Nov, up from 1,138 the day before; the National Republican Senatorial Committee asked all 82 counties to set aside affidavit ballots. [21] In Alaska the preliminary count has Mary Peltola on 102,962 and Sen. Dan Sullivan on 102,325. [22]
items.next: Mississippi's ballot-cure and mail-receipt deadline is 10 Nov and counties certify on 13 Nov; Alaska tabulates ranked-choice ballots on 18 Nov and certifies on 25 Nov. [23, 22]

items.h: Wang Yi receives a North Korean party secretary; three PLA sorties near Taiwan
items.body: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met Workers' Party secretary Kim Song-nam in Beijing on 5 Nov and said China would “resolutely” implement the “important consensuses” of Xi Jinping's June visit to Pyongyang. [24] On 6 Nov North Korea's foreign ministry “resolutely denounces and rejects” the Financial Action Task Force's decision to keep it blacklisted. [25] Taiwan counted three Chinese military aircraft sorties, nine navy ships and eight official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 6 Nov, against 21 sorties the day before. [26]
items.next: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders meet in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov.

items.h: The UN calls Abyei's drone strikes “a new and concerning dimension”
items.body: UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix told the Security Council on 5 Nov that drone strikes in Abyei, contested by Sudan and South Sudan, are “a new and concerning dimension”; strikes on 19 Oct killed at least 30. [27] In eastern Congo the army and allied Wazalendo fighters retook Mahanga and Kilongo in Masisi from the FRN, the Kabila-led successor to M23, Radio Okapi reports. [28] MONUSCO head James Swan, in Beni: “La protection des civils reste notre priorité.” [29]
items.next: The Sudan–South Sudan joint political and security mechanism meets in Khartoum on 8–10 Nov. [27]

feature.title: The board, 2–6 Nov: 37 entries across ten theatres
body: The board logged 37 entries from Monday to Friday morning. Russia–Ukraine, Iran, Taiwan and Sudan had an entry every day; the Sahel had one, Wednesday's report of Algerian troops escorting fuel trucks into Agadez, and Venezuela two, both from Washington: a Rubio meeting and Thursday's Cuba sanctions.

In Ukraine the week opened after the Oleshky truce expired on 1 Nov. On the night into 3 Nov Russia launched 289 drones and 59 cruise missiles; air defence downed 257 and 49. [30] The Komyshuvakha toll rose to 43 by Thursday. [16] Diplomacy ran in Brussels, at Thursday's White House event and toward Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov.

Around Hormuz, US strikes hit Qeshm Island on 2 Nov, Qatar carried a draft to Tehran, and the Revolutionary Guards claimed hits on tankers in reports on three days. On Thursday a senior Iranian official said a nuclear proposal had gone to Washington through Qatar, conditional on seven demands, and President Trump said of a decision on the war: “You'll know soon enough.” [17, 18]

In Asia, North Korea tested or fired missiles on 31 Oct, 2 Nov and 4 Nov and China's foreign minister received a senior North Korean party official, and Taiwan's daily count of Chinese aircraft ran from 49 sorties on Wednesday to three on Friday. [26] In Africa, the Sudan log carried an entry every day, most of them drone strikes on power stations, and on Thursday the UN peacekeeping chief told the Security Council that drones were “a new and concerning dimension” in Abyei. [27]

leads.title: Washington warns on fridge hacks as commissary freezers are probed
leads.teaser: Five US agencies told cold-chain operators to assume they are targets; DoD is looking at freezer failures in about six commissaries. Moscow calls the accusations “absurd”.
rows: On 5 Nov CISA, the FBI and the departments of Agriculture, Health and Human Services and Transportation issued joint guidance on hardening refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. CISA's Chris Butera: “Every organization that depends on refrigeration and monitoring systems should assume it could be a target.” [36]
About six US commissaries have had freezer malfunctions since late August, which the department is investigating as suspected hacks; nothing reported points to Europe. [36, 37]
A0. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov: “These are absurd statements and they, as always, have no argumentation or proof behind them.” [38] The EU's 4 Nov joint statement names no actor. [39]
leads.sw: Commissaries on our installations run the same class of remote-managed refrigeration: ask the garrison and the Defense Commissary Agency whether the joint guidance is applied at Brunssum, Geilenkirchen and Chièvres, and who answers a temperature alarm at night.

leads.title: Hoax bomb threats hit 27 flights on a third day, one at Brussels
leads.teaser: No device has been found anywhere. Fighters escorted airliners over France and Bulgaria; prosecutors in Prague have taken the case.
rows: At least 27 flights were disrupted on 5 Nov, the third day of threats; an Aer Lingus Dublin–Rome flight was diverted to the Évreux air base under fighter escort. [31]
LOT's LO235 from Warsaw received a threat and landed normally at Brussels, about 105 km from Heerlen; Belgian federal police are checking links to earlier cases. [32]
A0. EU Transport Commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas: it is “too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked.” [40]
leads.sw: Each hoax costs an escort, a diversion and a search at no cost to the sender, testing baseline requirement 7 (civil transportation): ask how a diversion to Geilenkirchen or Volkel would reach JFC Brunssum.

pattern: **Denial and warning on the same day:** the Kremlin called the fridge-attack accusations “absurd” as five US agencies told operators to assume they are targets. [38, 36]
**Aviation joins the target set:** hoax threats hit at least 27 flights on the wave's third day. [31]
**Courts and arrests:** Helsinki convicted the Fitburg's crew and Poland charged six over munitions parts for Kaliningrad. [33, 35]

week.t: **31 Oct – 6 Nov.** The refrigeration-controller wave set the week: stores in nine countries from 1 Nov, more than 100 by SecurityWeek's count, then French blood-plasma stores and UK meat processors; no government has attributed it. [41, 42] Latvia assessed one intruding drone as a Russian Geran-type and one as Ukrainian. [43] Proxy arrests ran in Germany and Poland, including the alleged organiser of the Starlink arson. [44, 45, 46] The last two days added hoax bomb threats against airliners, a Finnish conviction for the Fitburg cable cuts and six arrests over munitions parts smuggled into Kaliningrad. [31, 33, 35] Within 100 km of Heerlen the only confirmed case is still the Hoepertingen store. [47]

hybrid.note: Within 100 km of Heerlen there is no new case; the nearest event in the window is the threat to LOT's flight at Brussels Airport, about 105 km away. [32]

europe.h: De Wever calls the emergency budget a “dreadful failure” before seeing the King
europe.body: Prime Minister Bart De Wever told the Chamber on 5 Nov that Belgium will need an emergency budget for early 2027: “Voor de regering is dat een afschuwelijk falen”, for the government it is a dreadful failure. [48] Asked whether his resignation offer was sincere, he said “Ik meen altijd alles”, I always mean everything; MR president Georges-Louis Bouchez said the decision is the King's. [5] King Philippe receives De Wever again at 10:30 today.
europe.sw: SHAPE and NATO headquarters sit in Belgium; an emergency budget on provisional twelfths holds Belgian defence spending at this year's level.

europe.h: A Finnish court jails the Fitburg's captain for cutting two Baltic cables
europe.body: Helsinki District Court on 5 Nov convicted the Russian captain and Azerbaijani boatswain of the cargo ship Fitburg of aggravated criminal damage for the two Finland–Estonia telecom cables cut on 31 Dec 2025, sentencing them to 3 years 6 months and 2 years 10 months. [33] The court found the anchor was lowered deliberately and dragged about 130 km over the seabed; the captain intends to appeal. [34]
europe.sw: A conviction for an anchor drag is the Punish lever at sea; undersea cables carry baseline requirement 6 (resilient civil communications).

europe.h: Poland charges six with smuggling munitions parts into Kaliningrad
europe.body: Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) arrested five Poles and a Russian, special-services coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak announced on 5 Nov; the group smuggled military components including shell casings and projectiles worth more than PLN 2 million into Kaliningrad between June 2023 and December 2025, in vehicles with hidden compartments. Four face espionage charges and three months' pre-trial detention. The ABW: the group “illegally supplied Russia with significant quantities of components for military use.” [35]
europe.sw: The Kaliningrad line is in JFC Brunssum's area, and the smuggling roads through Lithuania are the reinforcement roads: ask the J2 whether the case files reach NATO counter-intelligence.

countries.h: Hungary's foreign minister calls Ukraine's EU entry by 2030 unrealistic
countries.body: In Vilnius on 5 Nov Foreign Minister Anita Orbán said of a 2030 accession date for Ukraine: “We do not think this is realistic.” She added: “We also do not support any fast-track entry”, while backing Ukraine's bid and citing a minority-rights agreement for Transcarpathia. [49]
countries.sw: Budapest backs Ukraine's bid but not its speed: Hungarian officials now separate support for Ukraine from support for a 2030 date, which shapes how J9 contacts in Budapest frame accession.

countries.h: Fico signs a cooperation declaration with Ukraine's prime minister in Lviv
countries.body: At government consultations in Lviv on 5 Nov, Robert Fico and Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi signed a joint declaration and a letter of intent on modernising border crossings. [50] Slovakia pledged €500,000 for 54 generators by the end of November, €300,000 for civilian shelters, €200,000 for hospital equipment and three locomotives. [51]
countries.sw: Generators, shelters and border crossings are civil-resilience aid under baseline requirements 1, 5 and 7, from a government that refuses military aid from state stocks.

countries.h: Slovakia's coalition is down to 75 secure votes of 150
countries.body: MP Roman Malatinec left the Strana vidieka grouping on 3 Nov for Tomáš Taraba's new party, leaving Smer, Hlas and the Slovak National Party with 75 secure votes of 150, though he says he stays in the coalition; votes were moved to Tue 10 Nov. [52] President Peter Pellegrini: early elections only if Fico decides so. [53]
countries.sw: A government one vote short of a majority sets Slovakia's 2027 defence budget; the 10 Nov votes are the first test.

countries.h: Germany names Lt Gen Christian Freuding as its next chief of defence
countries.body: Defence Minister Boris Pistorius named Lt Gen Christian Freuding, Inspector of the Army and former head of the Ukraine special staff, as Generalinspekteur from early February 2027, succeeding Gen Carsten Breuer, who chairs the NATO Military Committee from summer 2027. [54] The ministry credits Freuding with setting up the Army's first drone regiment. [55]
countries.sw: Germany's next chief of defence ran Berlin's Ukraine support and its first drone regiment, and his predecessor moves to NATO's top military committee post.

euregio.h: Schiphol doubles its stake in Maastricht Aachen Airport to 80% for €4 million
euregio.body: Royal Schiphol Group will buy 40% of Maastricht Aachen Airport in Beek, about 15 km from Heerlen, from the province for €4 million, taking its stake to 80%, and expects to invest €33 million; the province has put in more than €100 million since 2022. Provinciale Staten must approve. [56]
euregio.fy: Nothing changes for flights yet; the provincial vote is the date to watch.

euregio.h: Aachen closes Am Römerhof to through traffic for five weeks from Monday
euregio.body: From Mon 9 Nov Am Römerhof is closed to through traffic for about five weeks for sewer work, and the Forster Weg becomes two-way again; Regionetz cable work narrows lanes until January. [57]
euregio.fy: Allow extra time on Aachen's south side through mid-December.

items.h: The Netherlands launches a defence technology institute aimed first at the North Sea
items.body: Defensie launched the National Institute for Defence Technology (NIDT) on 5 Nov; its first challenge is round-the-clock protection of the North Sea with sensors and autonomous patrols, and it starts inside TNO. The ministry: “Met het NIDT ontstaat een brug tussen Defensie en de markt”, a bridge between Defence and the market. [58]
items.sw: North Sea pipelines and cables feed the energy and communications baseline requirements across the Benelux; an institute that buys autonomous patrols fast is a host-nation capability to know by name.

items.h: Lithuania tells the US it is ready to host more American troops
items.body: After meeting US Ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker at the Berlin Security Conference, Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas wrote on 5 Nov: “I assured him that Lithuania is ready to host additional US forces and provide the necessary infrastructure for their deployment.” The US presence, down to just over 100 in the summer, is back above 1,000 after two battalions arrived by late October. [59]
items.sw: Vilnius offers the infrastructure as Washington weighs cuts in Europe: a host-nation offer like this is what the posture review's option sets will be measured against.

items.h: Britain and the Netherlands push their joint amphibious ship programme “at pace”
items.body: In a joint statement on 4 Nov, UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and Dutch Defence Minister Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius committed to take the joint Amphibious Transport Ship programme forward “at pace” and to keep working together through the Multinational Force Ukraine and the multinational mission in the Strait of Hormuz. [60]
items.sw: Dutch and British marines train for NATO's northern flank together; a shared ship class fixes that amphibious lift for decades.

items.h: NATO opens a counter-drone marketplace: 16 systems, no further tender
items.body: NATO launched a counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) marketplace on 5 Nov from which allies can buy listed solutions “without any further tender process”. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) picked 16 static, transportable and on-the-move systems from five companies, Alta Ares, Axon Enterprise, Northrop Grumman, OSL UK and Quantum Systems, all already fielded in allied countries or Ukraine; the frameworks run 18 months and €3.1 million is set aside for more testing. Under the Drone Edge initiative allies have committed more than $40 billion to counter-drone capability over five years. [61]
items.sw: A framework buy without tender is the fastest route for a host nation to put counter-drone kit over a port or rail yard; check which of the 16 systems Dutch, German and Polish forces already field.

items.h: Rheinmetall cuts its 2026 guidance as artillery-ammunition acceptance slips
items.body: Rheinmetall's quarterly statement on 5 Nov puts nine-month sales at €8,376 million, up 38%, and the backlog at €78.0 billion, but cuts 2026 guidance to sales of about €13.2 billion and a margin of about 18.5%, citing delays to the Arminius Boxer project and to artillery-ammunition lot acceptance tests. [62] Ammunition sales guidance falls to €4.40–4.50 billion from €4.90–5.00 billion, and the shares fell as much as 16.3%. [63] Hensoldt the same morning raised its revenue forecast to about €2.8 billion. [64]
items.sw: Lot acceptance is the gate between a filled shell and a delivered one: half a billion euros less ammunition this year means fewer 155 mm rounds in allied stocks.

items.h: Shield AI agrees to buy counter-drone radar maker Echodyne for $5.3 billion
items.body: Shield AI agreed on 5 Nov to buy Echodyne, maker of solid-state radars that track small quadcopters, for $5.3 billion, $500 million of it tied to performance targets. [65] Echodyne won a $250 million counter-drone contract from Joint Interagency Task Force 401 in September. [66]
items.sw: Echodyne radars already sit in US counter-drone kits; one company now sells the sensor and the autonomy that base-defence buys in Europe would meet.

items.h: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, its first model rated Critical for cyber risk
items.body: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber on 5 Nov, a cybersecurity variant of GPT-6 Astra open only to vetted customers in its Daybreak Red programme. The system card rates it “Critical” for cybersecurity and reports 48.45% on ExploitGym against Astra's 42.43% and all 11 CyScenarioBench scenarios against Astra's 8. [67] OpenAI says it found 81 unknown Firefox flaws that Mozilla rated high severity. [68]

items.h: Google ships Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: 15-second video clips, 30% cheaper
items.body: Google made its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model generally available on 5 Nov in the Gemini API, AI Studio, Google Cloud, Vids and Flow. Clips run 3 to 15 seconds, up from 10, drafts render at 360p or 720p and upscale to 1080p or 4K, and the price is $0.07 a second at 720p, about $1.05 for a 15-second clip. Product manager Anish Nangia: “We have dropped the price 30% from Gemini Omni 1.1.” Outputs carry a SynthID watermark; no benchmark scores were published. [69]

items.h: Meta adds real-time voice and animated avatars to its Muse app in the US
items.body: Meta began rolling out voice conversations and expressive avatars in the Muse app on 5 Nov, on mobile, web and Mac in the US, powered by models it calls Muse Realtime Voice and Muse Realtime Avatar, with “hundreds of voices” and replies the user can interrupt. Voice for its AI glasses is “coming soon”. Meta published no latency or benchmark figures. [70]

Continuing resolution expires 11 Dec; one analyst puts a shutdown at 50%. [76]

words.where: Video posted on social media, filmed on the Pentagon's ceremonial steps
words.quote: Regardless of how people feel about the war, which I believe is a courageous and historic effort that will ensure Iran never gets nuclear weapons, we need to continue, as President Trump did in his first term, to rebuild our military.
words.context: His first statement on the midterms; he urged “every patriotic member of Congress” to back a $1.5 trillion budget. [71, 74]

words.where: Soldier's Medal ceremony, Fort Stewart, Georgia
words.quote: At extreme personal risk, they confronted, tackled, and restrained an active shooter. They absorbed the danger so their teammates wouldn't have to.
words.context: Presenting the Soldier's Medal to Sgts. Aaron Turner and Michael Boron of the 3rd Infantry Division for the August 2025 shooting on post. [77, 78]

depth.kind: Friday · The week's personnel and policy decisions
depth.title: 2–6 Nov: a space SOF command, a legal review and a Secretary under fire
body: Personnel news centred on one man: Secretary Hegseth vowed to fight renewed impeachment articles, which Rep. Massie refiles next week, and the President said he had “done a fantastic job”. [71, 72] Former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll joined OpenAI on 3 Nov. [79]

Policy moved by memo and release: a Space Force special operations component under SOCOM, a review of the military justice system, paid theology degrees for up to 75 future chaplains a year, more law-enforcement kit for the DC Guard, and $325 million in Office of Strategic Capital loans. [80, 81, 82, 83, 84] Still undecided: nominees for Army Secretary, Chief of Staff and AUTOWARCOM. [73]

head: Date
Decision
rows: Space Force special operations component under SOCOM [80]
Chaplain degree programme, up to 75 places [82]

dod.h: Hegseth vows to fight impeachment as Trump says he has done “a fantastic job”
dod.body: In a video on 5 Nov Secretary Hegseth called renewed impeachment articles “sham”: “You see, they attack me – they attack us – because we are effective. It's not going to work. We will not back down.” President Trump said he had “done a fantastic job”. [71] Rep. Thomas Massie plans to refile eight articles next week with a privileged resolution that forces a vote within two days. [72] The Europe force-level options are due today; none has been published.
dod.sw: The Europe options land on a Secretary facing an impeachment vote; a cut below the 76,000-troop floor still needs the assessment Congress requires first.

dod.h: The Iran war has pulled half of Yokosuka's destroyers to the Middle East
dod.body: Five of the ten destroyers based at Yokosuka and the carrier George Washington are in the Central Command area, some crews told they will not return until 2027, Defense One reported on 5 Nov; a Navy officer said the fleet expects a “17 DDG requirement” in the Middle East until 2029. [85]
dod.sw: Ships held in CENTCOM are ships missing from Europe's air and missile defence, and the posture review's promises to allies start from that arithmetic.

dod.h: Analysts warn drone-dominance funding could be cut to “a fraction” of $53.6 billion
dod.body: Byron Callan of Capital Alpha wrote on 5 Nov that drone dominance “could get shaved down to a ‘fraction’ of its $53.6 billion request” if Democrats write the FY2027 budget. [76] AUTOWARCOM still has no commander nominee. [73]
dod.sw: AUTOWARCOM and drone dominance are budget lines before they are commands: a smaller line means less counter-drone kit for EUCOM.

news.h: The Army tests a clip-on kit that lets drones drop 60 mm and 81 mm mortar rounds
news.body: The Munitions Air-dropped Lethal Effects Tool (MALET) from Picatinny's Armaments Center clips onto existing mortar rounds; the Army said on 4 Nov it passed a live-fire test dropping 60 mm rounds from a moving drone. No fielding date is set. [86]
news.sw: Drone-dropped mortar rounds are the threat base defence in Europe already faces; an Army version lets trainers replicate it at Grafenwöhr and Hohenfels.

congress.h: Five legislative weeks are left for the NDAA and defence appropriations
congress.body: When the lame duck opens on 9 Nov Congress has five legislative weeks; TD Cowen's Roman Schweizer said the NDAA and defence appropriations are “likely delayed until early 2027”, and Capital Alpha puts the chance of a shutdown when the stopgap expires on 11 Dec at 50%. [76] H.R. 8800 still sits in the Senate, and Lt. Gen. Kevin Admiral's nomination to USAREUR-AF (PN1188) is still Calendar No. 924. [73]
congress.sw: A funding lapse on 11 Dec puts PCS moves and non-essential travel across USAREUR-AF at risk; the stopgap, not the NDAA, is the date to plan against.

items.h: IRS sets 2027 tax figures: $33,200 standard deduction for joint filers
items.body: The IRS published its tax-year 2027 adjustments on 5 Nov: the standard deduction rises to $33,200 for joint filers, the foreign earned income exclusion to $137,300 and the health flexible spending limit to $3,500. TSP and 401(k) limits are not yet published; open seasons start Monday. [87]
items.fy: If anyone in the household earns non-military income abroad, the exclusion rises $4,400; hold January TSP changes until the IRS publishes the 2027 retirement limits.

dates: TRICARE and Federal Benefits open seasons open
2027 pay raise and tax-year 2027 adjustments take effect
career.note: Priority topics with nothing in the window: special operations; no remarks found from Caine, LaNeve or Grynkewich, and no leak of the posture options.

research.title: Lessons from Africa's Drone Wars (Africa Security Brief No. 49)
summary: Nate Allen argues that cheap, expendable drones are eroding the air-power advantage African governments have long held over armed groups, and that the continent's nonstate armed actors, more than its militaries, are exploiting the shift best. He points to Mali, where the government's Bayraktar TB2 fleet did not stop an assault, as a warning for capitals across the continent. [88]

Most armed groups still use drones to watch: JNIM, the Islamic State in West Africa and al Shabaab have had drone surveillance since 2018. JNIM's preferred strike method is the DJI Matrice 30T, which can carry two explosives. A handful of groups now field fibre-optic first-person-view (FPV) and one-way attack drones beyond what many state militaries can field; the brief reports the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) was the first African armed group to use fibre-optic FPV drones, against a base near Aguelhok, likely with Ukrainian help. In Sudan the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) used Chinese-made drones against Port Sudan, more than 1,000 km from territory they hold. [88]
Allen asks governments and partners to keep sensitive drone parts from being diverted to armed groups, and names pilot training as perhaps the biggest bottleneck for both sides. [88]
findings: **Since 2018:** JNIM, the Islamic State in West Africa and al Shabaab have flown drones for surveillance and reconnaissance; al Shabaab has not yet weaponised them. [88]
**Two explosives:** the load of the DJI Matrice 30T, JNIM's preferred delivery drone. [88]
**More than 1,000 km:** the distance from RSF-held territory to the Port Sudan airbases and infrastructure its Chinese-made drones struck. [88]
research.method: A policy brief built on open-source reporting; it publishes no dataset or strike count, so it cannot show how often each tactic is used, and claims of outside help rest on the reports it cites. The Africa Center's page refused the Readbook's request, so this summary rests on search extracts and carries no quotes.
research.sw: Fibre-optic FPV drones ignore the jammers most base-defence plans lean on: ask the force-protection cell which JFC Brunssum and host-nation sites rely on radio-frequency defeat alone.

aperture.inject: STARTEX + 1, 07:10. A commissary in the Benelux finds its freezers at +15 °C after the night, and an hour later a hoax bomb threat diverts an airliner to a military airfield in the Joint Operations Area. Stresses baseline requirements 4 (food and water) and 7 (civil transportation). First calls: the garrison and the host-nation food-safety authority, then the air desk.

deep.title: The Netherlands: €28.9 billion and a force of 100,000 by 2030
body: The host nation's 2027 defence budget is €28.9 billion: about €14.8 billion for people, operations and Ukraine, more than €3 billion of it for Ukraine, and €14.1 billion for equipment, innovation and real estate. Defensie counts about 85,000 people this year and aims for more than 100,000 by 2030. [92]

Two lines bear on civil-military work: the one-year Dienjaar expects about 1,500 recruits in 2027, and the national resilience training aims at 1,800 participants who then become reservists or take another role. The kit due in 2027 includes Foxtrot radios, Multi Missie Radars, a navy counter-drone system and the last of 28 modernised Apaches. [92] For host-nation support in Limburg the resilience pool matters more than the hardware: it is the reserve the civil plans can call on.

[91] Brent rose 3.9% after the Revolutionary Guards reported damaged tankers. [19] In Amsterdam BESI fell 7.3% and ASML 6.6%, but DSM-Firmenich rose 5.5% and the AEX lost only 0.6%. [90] The Bank of England raised its rate to 4.00% and US jobless claims fell to 189,000; the 10-year yield eased to 4.84%. [95, 6, 94]

items.h: Coalition leaders court the opposition one by one before Thursday's tax-plan vote
items.body: D66, VVD and CDA leaders are holding one-on-one talks with opposition parties for a tax-plan majority by early next week, NOS reported on 5 Nov; Pro and Volt want €1.5 billion shifted from tax on work to tax on wealth, which the VVD rejects. The Kamer votes on Thu 12 Nov; there is still no Eerste Kamer majority. [102]

items.h: KLM cuts 5,000 jobs, almost 15% of its staff
items.body: KLM will cut about 5,000 jobs through voluntary departures and not replacing leavers, and dropped a planned Airbus order, it said on 5 Nov. Chief executive Marjan Rintel: “het voortbestaan is geen vanzelfsprekendheid”, survival cannot be taken for granted. [103]

items.h: Gas falls 15% since the US vote and petrol is at its lowest since July
items.body: Dutch wholesale gas traded at about €88 a megawatt-hour on 5 Nov, down 15% since the US midterms, and the petrol advisory price fell below €2.50 a litre, the lowest since July. Suppliers wait to see whether a fall lasts before cutting tariffs: “De prijzen aan de pomp lopen achter op de olieprijs.” [101]

otd.title: On this day · 6 November 1944
otd.body: At about 02:30 German infantry ambushed engineers digging in by the Kall bridge below Kommerscheidt, and at 02:45 some 300 men of the 3d Battalion, 110th Infantry, left Germeter on foot for Task Force Ripple's attack to retake Schmidt. Not until 08:00 did the engineer group commander learn the Kall trail was cut; he ordered: “Get every man you have in line fighting.” The Kall gorge lies in the Hürtgen Forest, about 40 km from Heerlen. [116]

culture.title: Sint Maarten: lanterns on the eve of carnival
culture.body: On and around 11 November children in Limburg, Flanders and the Rhineland walk the streets with paper lanterns and sing Sint Maarten songs at doors for sweets; in German towns a rider dressed as St Martin, who shared his cloak with a beggar, often leads the Martinszug. Brunssum's Langeberg walks tonight and Monschau's villages from Tuesday. [7, 117] The same date opens carnival at 11:11, in Köln on the Heumarkt from 09:00. [118]

flags: Single-source or thin: the commissary freezer probe (Nextgov and TechCrunch citing officials; DoD has made no statement); Poland's six arrests (Euronews only); the hoax-threat count (Al Jazeera's 27 for Thursday; Euronews uses 27 for Tuesday); Iran's three damaged tankers (the IRGC via Reuters, no ship named, no CENTCOM comment); the Houthi claim on Dammam airport (Houthi statement via APA and Fox News, no Saudi confirmation); the Masisi recapture (Radio Okapi, local sources); the Freuding quotes (hartpunkt quoting the ministry; bmvg.de not reached); Sweden's border controls (Defence24 only); the Tapa blackmail case (ERR only); the AEX share moves (ad-hoc-news, tier 4); EU gas storage at 74.3% (Trading Economics, tier 4; the AGSI+ API needs a key); the Maastricht Aachen Airport price (L1 gives €4 million, De Limburger €4.2 million). Left out as single-source: Ukraine's wider private air-defence rules, Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small score, a $28.8 billion Shield AI valuation that appears only in a URL, and Handelsblatt's report that Berlin will buy half of KNDS. The research piece rests on search extracts of the Africa Center's text because africacenter.org refused the request (HTTP 403); quotes are kept out of it and its page length is not confirmed. Items from before the window, carried because no earlier edition had them: the Slovak coalition's loss of its secure majority (3 Nov), the UK–Netherlands joint statement (4 Nov) and 1st Infantry Division's role in Combined Resolve (army.mil, 4 Nov). Translations of Dutch, German, Slovak and French quotes are in the text. Priority topics with nothing in the window: special operations; no remarks found from Caine, LaNeve, Grynkewich or Rutte, and no leak of the posture options. Not reached: war.gov article, contract and transcript pages (403; the RSS feeds were used), jcs.mil, shape.nato.int, europeafrica.army.mil, tricare.mil, congress.gov web pages and the Senate Executive Calendar (nomination and bill data via api.congress.gov, which rate-limited after four calls), nato.int news listings, OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber launch post (403; the system card was used), the RENK release, arena.ai, the AFNORTH calendar PDF (403; rows carried from the 3 Nov check), the Labor Department claims PDF, bmvg.de, Aachener Zeitung, WDR, Het Belang van Limburg, RTBF regional pages and the Washington Post. The research desks' shared search budget ran out partway through, so instrumentalised migration, disinformation operations, arson and rail sabotage, the Sahel, Lebanon and Venezuela were checked only by direct page fetches: treat them as unchecked, not quiet. Not verified and left out: regional bus strikes from 17 Nov, Sint Maarten walks in Heerlen and Hoensbroek, and the Maastricht and Heerlen 11-11 details. Data checks: the ECB history ZIP's latest fix is 5 Nov, 1.1224 dollars per euro (USD/EUR 0.8909), appended to fx.json. Yahoo closes for 5 Nov appended to series.json, where Yahoo's final 4 Nov TTF close of €88.08 replaces €85.03 (see Corrections). minfin had posted no 6 Nov row by 05:48 CET, so ru-personnel-day and ru-uav-day end on 5 Nov; the Air Force tally for the night of 4–5 Nov (130 launched) is appended to ua-air, and the tally for the night of 5–6 Nov was not yet published. Lloyd's List's weekly counts start the hormuz-transits series, whose meta now describes them. canes.json: the 5–3 win at the Islanders appended; 13-3-2 and 28 points match the NHL standings; Nashville at Colorado was still in play and is marked pending. Saints: bye week, no change; Cardinals off-season. TVMaze: no change to any show. The Open-Meteo snow forecast was refreshed for all 12 resorts after two connection resets. events.json holds 42 live events after adding the Cannerberg tour and the Marres installation, two above the 40 ceiling, with nothing past its end date to prune. The FY27 colonel board recess date passed with nothing reported and was removed from the horizon; Neptune Strike 26-4 is marked complete on its scheduled end date, without a close-out release.
